fields.hero_prompt: Build a map quiz maker for my geography classes where students click places on a blank map and every answer is saved.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up map quiz maker?

quiz_plan.promise: the quiz plays the page's promise: a map quiz maker a visitor can take, whose results answer what the H1 says it builds

plan.angle: The top 10 splits into places to play (Lizard Point, Seterra, Geograck, a Google Play app) and quiz tools that describe maps in text or offer a geography template (AidaForm, GradeWithAI, BasedLabs). None shows a map quiz built on your own map, with every click saved to a table you can read. This page lets the searcher take a short quiz that names the map quiz to build, then shows four map quizzes a middle school, a courier company, a nature preserve, and a taproom run as their own app.
tab_stories: At Tamarack Middle School, Greta Osterhout's 84 students click all 50 states on a blank map, the results table shows Delaware missed by 39 of them, and she reteaches the Mid-Atlantic before the unit test.

Ruskmoor Couriers has each new driver click its 12 delivery zones on the city map before a first solo route; the pass mark is 11 of 12, 3 of 9 new hires fell short last week, and dispatcher Owen Takahara got an email naming them.

Hikers at Kestrel Bend Preserve answer an 8-question trail map quiz from the trailhead sign; across 1,120 tries this fall, 460 chose the Ridge Loop when the waterfall sits on the Creek Loop, so rangers mark the falls on the sign.
Brass Kettle Taproom runs a 10-pin world map round on trivia night, 16 teams answer on their phones, and the leaderboard ranks by score then time, with Lost Latitudes on top at 9 of 10.
